subject: Mutual Action Plan: procurement sequencing, DPA acceptance windows & go/no-go checkpoints
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@veridianhealth.com>, Veridian Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP and proposed sequencing for MSA/DPA/order form dependencies

Hi Samantha / Veridian team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per the ask — attached is a working MAP that ties evaluation milestones to the procurement/legal gates we discussed. Key items for your review:

- Evaluation window (pilot): 4 weeks starting 2026-04-01.
- DPA acceptance window: we propose formal sign-off during week 3 of the pilot to avoid a split acceptance window.
- MSA signature: target pre-commitment by 2026-05-01 to allow order form attachment before production onboarding.

I've included a short acceptance matrix (tab 2) that maps required security evidence to the DPA clauses. Karthik and Naomi are looped in to confirm sequencing and to flag any expectations from Redwood legal.

Next step requests:
1) Samantha — confirm whether Veridian needs the DPA redline before pilot kickoff or if a DPA-exception letter is acceptable for the pilot period.
2) Procurement — confirm PO lead times and any internal SLA gating (finance approval, signatory availability).

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + timeline), Redwood_MSA_draft.docx (clean MSA for reference), DPA_acceptance_matrix.pdf (evidence mapping).

Thanks,

Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior AM, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@veridianhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Veridian Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>, Adam Rios <adam.rios@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and proposed sequencing for MSA/DPA/order form dependencies

Mina — thanks for the swift turnaround and for the collateral. A couple immediate clarifications:

- We can start the pilot on 2026-04-01, but Veridian governance needs a signed DPA or an exec-approved temporary data handling addendum before any PHI-like test data is used. We can do an exception for synthetic or de-identified data, but we need written confirmation.
- PO process: procurement prefers having the PO issued after MSA signature but before order form execution; that is our standard. Lead time for PO is ~10 business days once we have final MSA + order form.
- Legal wants a short sequence diagram showing dates where DPA and MSA approvals are expected — can your team provide a single-slide artifact for the legal review?

We can agree in principle to your timeline but will require the DPA redline by 2026-04-08 for internal review. If Redwood needs to postpone DPA sign-off, we'll limit the pilot to anonymized data only.

I'll wait for the one-slide diagram and the final acceptance mapping.

Samantha
Samantha Cole
Senior Director, Procurement & Partnerships
Veridian Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Veridian Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and proposed sequencing for MSA/DPA/order form dependencies

Thanks, Samantha — good constraints to capture. Quick alignment from Redwood legal and program:

1) DPA approach: Redwood can issue a limited-scope DPA addendum that covers data handling for the pilot (no PHI ingestion) and a full DPA redline for signature prior to full production. We will annotate the DPA addendum to expire automatically once the full DPA is executed.

2) Sequence we recommend (minimal friction):
   - Week 0 (2026-04-01): Pilot kickoff using anonymized data + limited-scope DPA addendum (signed by both parties).
   - Week 2 (by 2026-04-15): Veri legal to complete initial review of full DPA redline (Redwood will provide annotated clause notes).
   - Week 3 (by 2026-04-22): Agreement on DPA redline OR formal list of open issues to allow escalation to execs.
   - Week 5 (by 2026-05-06): MSA signed and order form finalized; PO issuance window opens immediately after.

3) Attachments & evidence: We will upload the annotated DPA redline and a one-slide sequence diagram (PDF) to the shared Drive by COB 2026-03-23. The acceptance matrix maps exactly which audit artifacts Veridian needs for the DPA and which can be provided post-signature for the MSA orderform.

Open items for Veridian: confirm whether Veridian legal requires signed DPA before any test data is moved, or if anonymization + signed addendum is acceptable. Also, please confirm the PO approver name and whether they will be available during the Week 5 window.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@veridianhealth.com>, Veridian Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-24T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP and proposed sequencing for MSA/DPA/order form dependencies

All — quick check-in and approval of sequence. Naomi and I reviewed Karthik's plan and we authorize the limited-scope DPA addendum approach to unblock the pilot, provided:

- The pilot contains no PHI and Veridian signs the addendum with explicit expiration tied to full DPA execution.
- Redwood will provide the annotated DPA redline by 2026-03-23 (as promised) and will track open items in the MAP doc so legal can see progress per day.
- Operational readiness gate: a canary acceptance run (internal QA + Veridian checklist) is scheduled for 2026-05-10 — we will not move to production before that pass.

Mina — please resend the updated MAP with Karthik's sequence diagram embedded and the redline link visible in tab 4. Naomi — can you confirm the evidence items we will allow to be submitted post-MSA (non-blocking) vs those required before order form (blocking)?

Thanks — I want to keep the schedule tight but safe.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success & Delivery
Redwood Inference
